supplementary_materials: Data available on request ("The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.")

metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 ("computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores).")

nodes_source.source_quote: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: Real-world traffic video data and volumes collected from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. on the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao, used to calibrate the simulation.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Data availability statement explicitly states access is upon request from the corresponding author.

nodes_process.source_quote: Three consecutive frames of the traffic video in the controlled area are needed as the observation input.
nodes_process.description: Final result: DRL method reduces vehicle travel time by 13 percent. Initial logic and parameters are validated. Final transformation applied to extract vehicle locations and stack frames.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, tools not named, parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames... using the gradient-based algorithm Adam
nodes_process.description: Standard processing applied. Final transformation yields the trained Q-network policy for ramp metering.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, hardware tools named, all key hyperparameters stated in Table 1.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator.
nodes_process.description: Standard processing applied. Final transformation yields evaluation metrics and comparison against baselines.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, SUMO simulator named, simulation parameters and baseline parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: Standard processing applied. Final transformation yields travel time impact assessed by removing subarea data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curves for episode reward and mean travel time during the DRL training process.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Training process and parameters are detailed, but the underlying empirical traffic data is only available upon request, limiting full independent reproduction.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Vehicle travel times in the mainline across three scenarios: no control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Simulation setup in SUMO is well described, but the empirical data used to calibrate the simulation is not openly available.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Mean travel times across 20 simulation experiments for no controls, PI-ALINEA, and DRL, including percentage improvements.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Results are clearly aggregated from multiple random seed runs, but the base empirical dataset requires author request.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Temporal-spatial distribution of speed in the mainline for no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear visual mapping of simulated speeds; relies on empirical data available only on request.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Queue length at the on-ramp over time for no control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clearly plots queue lengths from the SUMO simulation; initial data available only on request.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios (i.e., the proportion of the red phase in the simulation time) in each simulation
nodes_sink.description: Relationship of queue length and red ratio for PI-ALINEA and DRL methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Correlates two simulated metrics well; limited by initial data availability.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Queue length and occupancy over time for PI-ALINEA and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Plots simulated metrics clearly; limited by initial data availability.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots of downstream volume in three scenarios (no control, PI-ALINEA, Deep RL) over time.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear aggregation of downstream volumes from SUMO simulation; data available on request.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_sink.description: Travel time with perturbed input data, comparing baseline to scenarios where specific subarea information is removed.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Perturbation method is described clearly; relies on the same base simulator and closed empirical data.
